events.question: Does it have a relation with sex?
events.note: An eyebrow is not a sexual organ and has no ordinary sexual function.

events.question: Does it work with electricity?
events.note: It is a natural body feature, not an electrical device.

events.question: Is it bigger than a foot?
events.note: A human eyebrow is smaller than a foot.

events.question: Does it go into the mouth?
events.note: It sits above the eye and is not ordinarily put into a mouth.

events.question: Is it made of metal?
events.note: It is an area of short human hairs.

events.question: Is it a toy?
events.note: It is an anatomical feature.

events.question: Can it be found in a store?
events.note: A natural eyebrow is not a retail item; cosmetics and imitations are excluded.

events.question: Is it natural?
events.note: Eyebrows grow naturally on people.

events.question: Is it part of the human body?
events.note: An eyebrow is part of human anatomy.

events.question: Does it have a skin?
events.note: The eyebrow is an area of hairs growing from skin above the eye.

events.question: Does it have bones?
events.note: The eyebrow hair-bearing feature itself has no bones; the underlying brow ridge is distinct.

events.question: Does it have a relationship with sexuality?
events.note: It is not normally classified as a sexual body feature; general attractiveness is too indirect.

events.question: Is it located on the face?
events.note: Eyebrows sit above the eyes on the face.

events.question: Do we usually want to get rid of it?
events.note: People generally keep their eyebrows, even if they trim or shape some hairs.

events.question: Is it used to listen to music?
events.note: Eyebrows do not provide hearing.

events.question: Can it breathe?
events.note: An eyebrow has no breathing function.

events.question: Does it have a relationship with eyes?
events.note: Eyebrows are directly above the eyes.

events.question: Does it watch TV?
events.note: Eyebrows do not see or watch things.

events.question: Is it hairy?
events.note: An eyebrow consists of a patch of short hairs.

events.question: Can it be opened or closed?
events.note: Eyebrows can move but do not open or close like eyelids.

events.question: Does it belong to a specific person?
events.note: The target is the general human eyebrow feature, with no particular person specified.

events.question: Does it usually go by two?
events.note: People usually have two eyebrows.

events.question: Is it worn on the forehead?
events.note: Interpreted as location: eyebrows are at the lower forehead above the eyes, although they grow there rather than being worn.

events.question: Is it double?
events.note: Interpreted as occurring as a pair: humans normally have two eyebrows.

events.question: Did it exist in 1948?
events.note: Humans had eyebrows in 1948.

events.question: Is it something that can be trimmed?
events.note: Eyebrow hairs can be trimmed.

events.question: Do some radio hosts have it?
events.note: Radio hosts are people and generally have eyebrows.

events.question: Is it smaller than a coin?
events.note: A complete adult eyebrow is usually longer than an ordinary coin diameter, though width and size vary.

events.name: An eyebrow
events.note: Exact match to the human eyebrow feature.
